Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Technologies Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for those attending the conference call by phone will be announced once the presentation concludes. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet Technologies' results for the second quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; Chris Wong, VP of Sales; and Dana Ellis, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report another strong quarter for SecureNet Technologies. Our results reflect the growing importance of cybersecurity in today's digital landscape and our ability to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The market reception to AegisXDR has been overwhelmingly positive, significantly contributing to our 28% year-over-year revenue growth.

Our strategy is built on seven key pillars: excelling in marketing spend efficiency to scale effectively, leveraging channel partner performance for revenue acceleration, driving innovation through recent product and feature launches, demonstrating the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, expanding the number of customers with ARR over $100,000, outperforming on billings versus guidance, and providing sharp commentary on the evolving threat landscape.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $275 million in the second quarter, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained healthy at 78%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $190 million. Net income was $42 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.60. We are raising our full-year revenue guidance to $1.15 billion to $1.18 billion and earnings guidance accordingly based on our strong performance to date.

To give more color on our momentum, let me touch on the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, which has been the engine driving these exceptional results and positions SecureNet at the forefront of the cybersecurity industry. Our GTM is built on a hybrid model blending high-touch enterprise sales, scalable channel partnerships, and product-led growth motions tailored to the evolving threat landscape, including ransomware proliferation, state-sponsored APTs, and the shift to zero-trust and cloud-native architectures.

Headline metrics underscore this success: our ARR reached $285 million at quarter-end, up 52% year-over-year and 14% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by 420 net new customers—a 38% YoY increase—with an average ACV of $620,000, up from $540,000 last year, reflecting our pivot toward larger enterprise deals in SASE and XDR bundles. CAC payback improved to 9 months from 12 months ago, thanks to optimized inbound lead gen from our Threat Intelligence Portal, now with 1.2 million monthly active users and a 28% conversion rate to trials. NRR held strong at 128%, driven by 42% expansion revenue from customers upsellling into our AI-powered XDR platform, AegisXDR 2.0, which integrates seamlessly with EDR leaders like CrowdStrike Falcon and Microsoft Defender.

Our channel-first approach now accounts for 62% of bookings, up from 48% last year. We've deepened alliances with hyperscalers and distributors: AWS Marketplace generated $42 million in ARR this quarter, a 75% YoY surge, capturing share in the booming cloud security market projected by Gartner to grow 25% CAGR through 2027. Our expanded partnership with Snowflake for data-centric security delivered 15 deals averaging $1.2 million ACV, tapping into the 40% rise in supply chain attacks tracked via our SecureNet Labs reports. Win rates against competitors: 68% versus Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Cloud, 72% against Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, and 81% in greenfield XDR opportunities where our ML-driven behavioral analytics outpace legacy SIEMs like Splunk.

Regionally, Americas represent 58% of revenue, adding 210 logos with federal sector bookings up 90% YoY post-FedRAMP High authorization. EMEA contributed 26%, growing 61% YoY, propelled by GDPR and NIS2; our London team closed 25% more deals, including a €15 million contract with a Big Four bank for MDR. APAC, 16% of the mix, exploded 89% YoY, thanks to PDPA compliance and our Tokyo data center, outpacing IDC's 22% regional market growth.

We've leaned into technical initiatives like the Q1 launch of AegisXDR 2.0, with its GenAI threat hunting engine processing 10 petabytes daily across 50,000 endpoints per customer, shortening sales cycles by 22% to 140 days via self-serve PoCs. Our free-tier EPP converted 35% of 150,000 sign-ups to paid, optimized for SMBs. Amid 32% YoY ransomware surge per our Q2 Threat Report, demand for Autonomous Response spiked 55%, with 70% attachment rates.

Forward, we're allocating $50 million to GTM enhancements: 120 new reps for mid-market verticals like healthcare, up 45% pipeline QoQ post-Change Healthcare, and a partner-led MDR program with Deloitte targeting $100 million pipeline. Our rule of 40 score hit 92, validating this as a moat-builder in a $200 billion TAM at 14% CAGR.

Another key leading indicator is our number of customers generating over $100K in ARR. This cohort drives outsized NRR at 118% and validates our land-and-expand model amid ransomware-as-a-service and GenAI security blind spots post-ChatGPT.

We ended Q2 with 452 such customers, a 19% YoY increase from 380 and 8% sequential from 419 in Q1, outpacing overall customer growth of 12% YoY. They account for 68% of total ARR, up from 62%, underscoring our shift to complex deployments in a $200B+ TAM by 2028 per Gartner.

By segment: Enterprise (Fortune 1000 equivalents) added 22 net new to 187 total, up 24% YoY, fueled by ZTNA integrations at a top-5 global bank; our ML anomaly detection cut false positives 40% post-Log4j/MOVEit. Mid-market grew to 265, up 16% YoY, via channel like TD Synnex and Azure co-sells amid 30% SMB ransomware rise per Sophos.

Regions: North America 312 (69%), up 15% YoY, anchored by healthcare wins like a $250K expansion vs. Ryuk variants. EMEA surged to 89, 38% YoY on NIS2, landing DACH/UK logos with EU Cloud Sovereignty. APAC hit 51, 29% YoY via NTT for SASE against Salt Typhoon.

65% expansions from upsells to SASE or Agentic AI Response Orchestrator at 95% phishing containment. Churn sub-2% vs. industry 5-7%. Expect 490-500 by Q3 end, 15-20% YoY growth, ramping quantum-resistant crypto.

On billings, we came in exceptionally strong at $312 million, a 12% sequential increase from Q1 and 28% YoY, exceeding our $285 million midpoint guidance by 9% and 7% above the high end.

Billings lead future revenue under our 92% subscription model, up from 88% YoY, amid 35% ransomware surge per Chainalysis and Change Healthcare fallout.

By segment: Cloud Security 42% at $131 million, 35% YoY, from NexShield CloudGuard SSE wins like a top-5 hyperscaler deal for 200,000 developers; DBNER 128% with GenAI blocking 97% novel attacks. Endpoint/XDR $112 million, 36%, 25% YoY, 92% activation, NRR 115%. Network/emerging $69 million, 18% YoY.

Regions: Americas $192 million (62%), 32% YoY; EMEA $68 million, 22% YoY on NIS2; APAC $52 million, 45% YoY with $10M+ critical infra deals.

Validates our Unified Platform thesis in $215B 2024 spend per Gartner; NexShield AI Sentinel cut MTTR 65% vs. Splunk. Multi-year mix 68%, deferred rev $1.8B.

Raising FY24 billings to $1.22-1.25B, 25-30% YoY; Q3 $315-325M.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. Our technology roadmap is focused on delivering next-generation security solutions that leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas of focus include our recent product and feature launches, which have driven Q2 performance and underscore our leadership amid ransomware up 37% YoY per Chainalysis, APT41 threats, and hybrid work Zero Trust needs. We've responded with three major launches since Q1, leveraging AegisAI processing 10 trillion signals daily.

First, AegisXDR 2.0 launched in May: quantum leap in XDR with autonomous SOAR and predictive analytics, 99.8% MITRE mapping, GenAI playbooks cutting MTTR to under 15 minutes. Fortune 50 finance and U.S. healthcare adopters saw 62% alert fatigue reduction, 45% faster remediation. Drove $28M new ARR, 18% of 32% subscription growth; NPS 78 from 65; 240 net logos, 40% EDR upsell.

In July, Aegis ZeroTrust Edge SASE with ZTNA 2.0, eBPF micro-segmentation for multi-cloud, post-quantum ready post-Log4Shell. Q2 bookings $45M, 150% YoY; $12M NATO deal. NA 55%, APAC 3x growth via Singtel vs. supply chain attacks; EMEA 28% on GDPR/NIS2.

August's RansomShield Rollback, free Enterprise upgrade: immutable snapshots, AI decryption in <2 hours, >95% success vs. Cohesity/Rubrik, integrated deception luring to honeyfiles. Protected 1,200 endpoints, $150M losses averted amid 21% double-extortion per Sophos; warranty attach 72% from 45%, +$15M services ARR.

These position us vs. CrowdStrike Falcon, Palo Alto Cortex in $50B+ XDR per IDC, stealing from Zscaler ZTNA. Co-sell with AWS/Microsoft drove 25% pipeline; freemium EDR-XDR 35% conversion. FY25 $200M R&D for quantum/OT/IoT, $15B ICS market. Singapore DC Q1 for APAC. Delivered 22% revenue beat, TAM +15% to $8.5B, 85% gross retention, 128% NRR. We're defining resilient cybersecurity.

Morgan Patel: We are committed to providing our customers with the highest level of security. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect against emerging threats. To contextualize our strong results—revenue up 28% YoY to $275 million, ARR +35%—against this hostile environment, our Q2 Threat Intelligence Report from 12,000 customers and 4.5 trillion daily events shows ransomware up 142% YoY, payouts >$4.5M from $3.2M; Chainalysis H1 $1.1B payments. Sophistication: 210% multi-stage living-off-the-land, evading EDR.

AI supercharges threats: adversarial phishing bypasses 92% gateways, deepfakes +300% like MGM. Supply chain +175% post-SolarWinds/MOVEit, 68% unpatched OSS like Log4j. Cloud misconfigs 55%, boosting CNAPP 45% bookings.

Regions: NA (52% rev) ransomware +160%, healthcare/infra vs. FTC. EMEA +130% APTs, Ukraine hybrid; NATO Sovereign Cloud. APAC +42% rev, SE Asia mobile malware +250% on 5G/IoT; China data localization.

We're architecting ahead: Zero Trust Edge SASE UEBA cuts lateral detection to 90 seconds, Gartner 4.8/5. Post-quantum Kyber-768 in VPN vs. harvest-now-decrypt. Microsoft Sentinel/Fabric 30% logos; CrowdStrike Falcon Fusion SOAR.

IDC $225B market by 2027, XDR/AI 32% CAGR. $2.5B RPO +40%, 65% expansions threat-driven. FY24 rev $6.0-6.2B? Wait, scaled to our size: positioned to outpace as threats compound.

Chris Wong: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners. Diving deeper, our channel partner ecosystem drove 68% of total revenue, up from 62% YoY and 65% Q1, or $187 million of $275 million, with channel ARR $720M at 118% NRR from MDR expansions. Global market to $250B by 2028 per Gartner; partners extend salesforce for AegisXDR and SecureEdge SASE vs. LockBit RaaS, zero-trust hybrid work.

Top Platinum/Gold (450+, CDW, Insight, TD SYNNEX, Ingram) 82% channel rev $153M, avg ACV $450K +15% YoY bundling with Palo Alto firewalls, Microsoft Sentinel. Silver/Bronze (2,100+) 18% mid-market.

Regions: Americas 52% $97M, 32% YoY on CISA zero-trust, HIPAA; AWS Marketplace $22M +45% QoQ. EMEA 31% $58M, 26% YoY GDPR/NIS2; Bechtle/Computacenter SecureEdge POCs 72% conversion. APAC 17% $32M, 24% YoY MSPs like Brennan IT with CrowdStrike synergies post-MOVEit.

Subscription-led 92% deals + dollar expansion; 40% multi-product (2.8 avg), AegisXDR + Phantom Lure ML honeypots vs. T1566 phishing.

Invested in PartnerSync Academy: 1,200 engineers certified on API/SOAR MITRE T1566. Channel Accelerator $15M MDF, 35% new logos Azure/Google; Elite MDR Alliance 50 MSPs $42M rev 95% margins white-label SOC.

Expect 70-72% FY24 rev, Q3 $210-220M. Mitigate supply via software; +20% rebates high-NRR. Velocity: cycles 120 to 90 days, Partner Portal 88% closure accuracy.

Thriving channel outpaces Zscaler/Fortinet mindshare.

Dana Ellis: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events. As a critical lever for scaling in this hyper-competitive landscape—with ransomware +37% YoY per Chainalysis, APT41 supply chain post-SolarWinds—we've prioritized high-ROI channels for enterprise pipeline.

Q2 marketing spend $148M, +12% YoY from $132M amid 28% rev to $912M wait, aligned to $275M scale but efficiency: Marketing Efficiency Ratio (nACV/marketing $) 5.8x, +22% from 4.8x Q2'23, + seq from 5.4x Q1'24, ahead industry 4.2x, closing on CrowdStrike 6.1x per G2/Sirius.

CAC new logos -18% to $42K from $51K; LTV/CAC 4.9x from 3.7x; payback 11 mo from 14; marketing-sourced margin 68% +400bps, optimized net new ARR.

Precision pivot: ABM 42% spend from 32%, 8.2x ROAS via 6sense/Demandbase on 1,200 Tier 1 (Fortune 1000 finance/infra); post-MOVEit 'Breach Readiness' $56M pipeline, 8 mo payback tied SecureNet Threat Exchange.

Digital/performance 28% $41M, 6.4x ROAS LinkedIn/Google 'AI EDR'/'SSPM'; FalconML AI scoring +Salesforce Einstein/Marketo, lead-opp +31% to 24%, 47 signals Bombora/DarkOwl, filter 62% low leads.

Content/thought 18%, 4.9x via CyberPulse webinars, Forrester quantum crypto. Partnerships/events 12%, Black Hat/RSA, AWS/Azure co-marketing 15% pipeline SecureNet Defender.

MOC Q4'23 unifies attribution multi-touch, -27% dark funnel, 92% closed-won touchpoints from 71%, GDPR/CCPA server-side.

Regions: NA 6.4x MER $92M (62%), 214 logos CAC $38K, CMMC/Carahsoft federal. EMEA 5.2x +19% $32M NIS2/DORA; DACH ABM post-Cloudflare 18% conv; French Zero Trust €24M post-Olympics. APAC/Japan 4.7x $24M +28% rev ASD/My Number SASE; LINE/WeChat SMB CAC -24% $39K, forex -2pts.

Threat-led growth: 65% Q3 budget upsell/cross 4,200 base, 42% AI Sentinel attach +35% LTV.

Q3 spend $155-160M, 5.9-6.2x; GenAI nurture GPT-4o pilot. Risks ad fatigue/CPRA, but 10B daily signals moat.

Firing on all cylinders for 32% FY24 ARR growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session: If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. Limit your questions to one per caller. We'll pause 10 seconds after the question to allow note-taking. First question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Thompson: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, could you speak to how the seven pillars are positioning the company for the back half and any adjustments to long-term strategy?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, these pillars are interconnected and giving us durable momentum. From marketing efficiency gains to channel acceleration and product innovation, we're seeing compounded effects—like 128% NRR across high-value customers. No major shifts; we're doubling down on AI-native platforms to capture expanding TAM amid persistent threats. Confident in delivering sustained hypergrowth.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great results. Jordan, on the raised guidance, can you walk through the key assumptions, especially around billings and macro impacts?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Lisa. FY billings now $1.22-1.25B reflects continued execution on GTM, with broad strength in cloud/endpoint. Assumes resilient demand despite macro—federal steady, APAC accelerating—but builds in EMEA FX caution. Q3 $315-325M sequential uptick from multi-year mix. Rule of 40 at 92 gives operating leverage.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Solid pipeline metrics. Taylor, on the roadmap, how are AegisXDR and ZeroTrust Edge performing in pilots versus competitors, and any new features for Q3?

Taylor Kim: Thanks, Raj. Pilots converting at 35% freemium, outpacing peers on MTTR <15 min and 95% rollback success. Q3 agentless cloud workload protection and quantum encryption ramping, enhancing multi-cloud ZTNA. Early NATO/ hyperscaler feedback 99.8% MITRE accuracy—positioned for $50B XDR share.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emily Rodriguez: Thanks. Morgan, with ransomware sophistication up, how is SecureNet adapting security posture for customers, particularly in supply chain and AI threats?

Morgan Patel: Emily, our global sensors track 4.5T events daily, feeding AegisAI for proactive UEBA/SOAR. RansomShield + deception thwarts lateral movement; post-quantum VPNs counter harvest attacks. 65% expansions cite our threat intel—churn <2% as we automate 95% containment. Customers like healthcare nets averting $150M losses.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident in our ability to deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
